name: KY-005 infrared LED transmitter module
description: 940 nm infrared LED transmitter module: a single 5 mm IR LED with a series current-limiting resistor, no driver transistor. Drive the S pin high and the LED emits invisible infrared light; low switches it off. To control a TV or air-conditioner, switch it with 38 kHz carrier bursts in the remote's protocol timing (e.g. NEC). The LED current (about 20-30 mA from a GPIO) comes from the S pin. Sold as: Keyes / HW-489 KY-005 infrared transmitter module from the 37-in-1 sensor kits, 3-pin header S, (middle, unlabelled VCC), -.
eli5: The light in a TV remote: set the pin high and it glows with infrared light your eyes cannot see (a phone camera can). Flick it on and off in the right pattern and a TV obeys it.

pins.name: S
pins.description: Signal: high = IR LED on, low = off. Drives the LED through the on-board resistor, so this pin supplies the LED current.

pins.name: MID
pins.description: Middle pin, unlabelled VCC (3.3-5 V). The LED itself runs between S and -, so this pin is not needed to make it emit.
Ground (LED cathode), shared with the microcontroller

buildNotes: Wire S to a GPIO and - to GND. The middle pin (VCC) is optional; the LED runs from S through the on-board resistor.
Check that your board has the small series resistor next to the LED. Some clones leave it out: then add a 100-220 Ohm resistor in series with S or the LED and the GPIO can be damaged.
Range is 1-3 m at GPIO current (20-30 mA). For more range switch it with an NPN transistor (2N2222 or BC547, 1 kOhm base resistor) and feed the LED from 5 V.
On a Raspberry Pi Pico or Raspberry Pi (about 12-16 mA per pin) use the transistor circuit for anything beyond a short-range test.
Infrared is invisible: point a phone camera at the LED to see it flash. Do not stare into it at close range.

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time

ir = Pin({S}, Pin.OUT, value=0)  # S high = IR LED on (check it with a phone camera)
while True:
    ir.value(1)
    print('IR ON')
    time.sleep(1)
    ir.value(0)
    print('IR OFF')
    time.sleep(2)

test.title: The IR LED switches on, then off again
